userStories.title: Map tool-result images to the model wire format
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Allow nax-ai to send images in tool results to vision models and represent them as notes for text-only models.

**Motivation** — pi-ai 1.5.0 (the version nax-ai pins) already accepts `ImageContent` in a `toolResult` message (`ToolResultMessage.content: (TextContent | ImageContent)[]`), and its OpenAI completions, OpenAI responses and Google providers already route tool-result images on vision models; nax's own types drop the image at every seam before it gets there.

**Approach** — The `tool-result` variant of `ConversationMessage` (`packages/nax-ai/src/protocols/types.ts`) gains `readonly images?: readonly ImageAttachment[]`, the type user messages already use. `toPiMessages` (`packages/nax-ai/src/protocols/pi-client.ts`, reached through `toPiContext(req, model)`, which the module exports and tests import by path) maps a tool result with a non-empty `images` list to pi-ai content `[{ type: "text", text: content }, ...images.map(({ data, mimeType }) => ({ type: "image", data, mimeType }))]` when `model.input` includes `"image"`. When the model does not accept image input, the images are left out and one note line per image is appended to the text: `[image not shown: this model does not accept image input (image/png 1280x720)]`, or `(image/png)` when width or height is absent. Only `type`, `data` and `mimeType` reach the wire; `width`, `height` and `source` never do. A result with no images, or `images: []`, maps exactly as today. This is the one place nax decides vision support for a tool-result image, so a session that switches to a text-only model mid-conversation degrades the same way. Preserve `isError` and map images even when a directly supplied protocol result has `isError: true`. Extend `packages/nax-ai/test/protocols/pi-client-images.test.ts` for the tool-result cases. Every mapping fixture includes an earlier assistant tool call whose ID matches the result; keep the existing orphan-result error unchanged.

**Scope** — In: protocol type, wire mapping, and mapping tests for tool-result images. Out: native runtime and request plumbing (US-002), persistence (US-003), image detection (US-004), and run/hop plumbing (US-007). User-image mapping and provider implementations are unchanged. ACP stays unchanged.

**Interface**
```typescript
{ role: "tool-result"; toolCallId: string; content: string; isError?: boolean; readonly images?: readonly ImageAttachment[] }
```
acceptanceCriteria: When toPiContext receives a model with input ["text", "image"], an assistant tool call "c1" named "Read", and its tool-result with content "shot" and images [PNG A (data "AAAA", 2x2), JPEG B (data "BBBB")], then the pi toolResult content equals [{ type: "text", text: "shot" }, { type: "image", data: "AAAA", mimeType: "image/png" }, { type: "image", data: "BBBB", mimeType: "image/jpeg" }].
When toPiContext maps a tool result for a vision model and the source attachment carries width, height and source, then each pi toolResult image part has exactly the keys type, data and mimeType.

When toPiContext receives a model with input ["text"], an assistant Read tool call "c1", and its tool result with content "shot" and PNG A (data "AAAA", 2x2), then the entire pi toolResult content equals the single part [{ type: "text", text: "shot\n[image not shown: this model does not accept image input (image/png 2x2)]" }].

When toPiContext maps a tool result with a JPEG attachment lacking width and height for a text-only model, then the appended note line equals `[image not shown: this model does not accept image input (image/jpeg)]`.

When toPiContext maps a tool result with content "shot" and images [PNG A (2x2), JPEG B (no dimensions)] for a text-only model, then its pi toolResult content is one text part containing exactly `shot\n[image not shown: this model does not accept image input (image/png 2x2)]\n[image not shown: this model does not accept image input (image/jpeg)]`, preserving image order with one note per line after the original content.
When toPiContext maps a tool result with content "shot" and no images key for a vision model, then the pi toolResult content equals [{ type: "text", text: "shot" }].
When toPiContext maps a tool result with content "shot" and images: [] for a vision model, then the pi toolResult content equals [{ type: "text", text: "shot" }].
When toPiContext maps a tool result with isError: true and one image for a vision model, then the pi toolResult has isError: true and the image part after the text.

routing.reasoning: One additive protocol field and a localized mapping with existing Vitest fixtures and no dependency change.

userStories.title: Carry native tool-result images through the turn loop
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Carry successful tool-result images through native execution into model requests and account for them in request capping and compaction.

**Motivation** — Asked to check a screenshot, a vision-capable model answered that no tool feeds an image into its input and fell back to computing pixel statistics with Bash.

**Approach** — Each seam that today copies only `content` carries `images` too:

- `ToolResult` (`tools/registry.ts`) gains `readonly images?: readonly ImageAttachment[]`.
- `CodingToolOutcome`'s `ok` / `error` arm (`tools/runtime.ts`) gains `readonly images?: readonly ImageAttachment[]`. `callTool`'s success path puts `result.images` on the outcome when `kind` is `"ok"` and the list is non-empty, on both the immediate and the `deferModelTruncation` return. An `"error"` outcome never carries images. `runtime.ts` is 599 lines against the 600-line source cap, and `runTool` is baselined at complexity 24 in `packages/nax-agent/scripts/baselines/complexity-baseline.json` (strict limit 20): the story moves the outcome assembly into a helper module and puts the images conditional there, so neither the file nor `runTool` grows; if the extraction lowers `runTool`'s score, the baseline entry is lowered to match.
- `AdapterInteractionResponse` (`session/interaction-handler.ts`) gains `images?: readonly ImageAttachment[]`; `answerFor` (`session/session-interaction.ts`) copies a non-empty `outcome.images`.
- In `turn-tool-batch.ts` the `after_tool` event still shapes `content` only (its patch whitelist stays `["content", "isError"]`); the images ride beside it: `buildToolResult` gains `images?` and spreads it in only when non-empty, the same absent-stays-absent rule `isError` follows. `ToolResultMessage` and the second `tool-result` arm of `TranscriptMessage` (`native/session/compaction.ts`) gain `readonly images?: readonly ImageAttachment[]`. The error path (`catch`) builds its result without images.
- `capRequestImages` (`native/session/image-context.ts`) counts tool-result images with user images in one newest-first pass against `MAX_REQUEST_IMAGES` and `MAX_REQUEST_IMAGE_BASE64_CHARS`; a dropped tool-result image becomes the note `[image from an earlier turn dropped from context: <mimeType>]` appended to that tool result's content, as for a user image.
- `imagesAsNotes` turns tool-result images into `[image: <mimeType> <w>x<h>]` lines appended to the tool result's content, as it does for user images.
- `estimateTokens` (`compaction.ts`) counts a tool result's images with the same per-image estimate it uses for a user message, through one `imageTokens(images)` helper both arms call (it scores 14 today; copying the loop would push it near the limit).
- `capRequestImages` scores 17 against the strict limit of 20: its per-message keep/drop step moves into a helper shared by the user and tool-result arms. Every new helper scores 20 or less, and no new complexity-baseline entry is created for `image-context.ts` or `compaction.ts`.

Embedder tools (`runEmbedderTool`) keep answering `{ answer: result.content }`. Extract outcome assembly into the existing `packages/nax-agent/src/tools/runtime-calltool.ts` helper module; keep imports of runtime types type-only so the helper does not introduce a cycle. `BuildToolResultArgs` is declared with `ToolResultMessage` in `native/session/tool-result.ts`; copy the successful answer's image list separately from the plugin patch without changing which `isError` patches are allowed. Add cases to the existing `test/unit/tools/runtime.test.ts`, `test/unit/native/session/turn-tool-batch.test.ts`, `image-context.test.ts` and `image-compaction.test.ts` suites, and add `test/unit/native/session-adapter-tool-images.test.ts`. Use the handler/runtime composition from `test/unit/native/session-adapter-abort-reasons.test.ts`, not its abort-only model stub: grant tool T under the fixture policy, advertise it in `sendTurn`, capture the second model request, and end its response without another tool call. If `runTool` improves, lower only its entry in the agent complexity baseline.

**Scope** — In: native result, outcome, response, transcript message and request shaping seams, runtime helper extraction, and unit and two-round-trip integration coverage; preserve text audit and plugin semantics. Out: protocol mapping (US-001), sidecar persistence (US-003), actually producing images in Read (US-004), and the separate run/hop handler (US-007). Images from tools other than `Read` (Bash output, MCP tool results, embedder tools): only `Read` produces tool-result images. Showing tool-result images in the chat TUI transcript: the Read card shows the result's text line only. ACP stays unchanged.

**Interface**
```typescript
// ToolResult, CodingToolOutcome's ok/error arm, ToolResultMessage, BuildToolResultArgs, and TranscriptMessage's second tool-result arm
readonly images?: readonly ImageAttachment[]
// AdapterInteractionResponse
images?: readonly ImageAttachment[]
function buildToolResult(args: BuildToolResultArgs): ToolResultMessage
```
acceptanceCriteria: When runtime.callTool runs a registered tool returning { content: "x", images: [PNG A] }, then it resolves to an outcome matching { kind: "ok", content: "x", images: [PNG A] }.

When runtime.callTool runs a registered tool returning { content: "x", images: [PNG A] } with call context { deferModelTruncation: true }, then it resolves to an outcome carrying images equal to [PNG A] and a callable finalizeAudit field.
When runtime.callTool runs a tool returning { content: "bad", isError: true, images: [PNG A] }, then it resolves to a kind: "error" outcome with no images key.
When runtime.callTool runs a tool returning { content: "x", images: [] }, then its outcome has no images key.
When buildToolResult receives { toolCallId: "c1", content: "x", images: [PNG A] }, then the message has images equal to [PNG A].
When buildToolResult receives { toolCallId: "c1", content: "x" } or the same args with images: [], then the message has no images key in either case.

Given NativeSessionAdapter.sendTurn with the production createSessionInteractionHandler over createCodingToolRuntime({ extraTools: [T] }) as in session-adapter-abort-reasons.test.ts, and a stub model that calls T first and ends on the second response, when T returns { content: "x", images: [PNG A] }, then the second request's tool-result for the call has images equal to [PNG A].
Given that same native turn composition and T's image result, when an after_tool handler patches content to "y", then the second request's tool-result matches { content: "y", images: [PNG A] }.
Given that same native turn composition, when T throws, then the second request's tool-result for T has no images key.

When capRequestImages receives [user with 15 images, tool-result with 10 images], then it returns the two messages with all 10 tool-result images, the newest 10 user images, and exactly five [image from an earlier turn dropped from context: image/png] lines appended to user content.

When capRequestImages receives [tool-result with 15 images, user with 10 images], then it returns the two messages with all 10 user images, the newest 10 tool-result images, and exactly five [image from an earlier turn dropped from context: image/png] lines appended to tool-result content.

When capRequestImages receives user and tool-result attachments whose combined base64 length exceeds MAX_REQUEST_IMAGE_BASE64_CHARS, then the combined base64 length of all kept images is at or below MAX_REQUEST_IMAGE_BASE64_CHARS.
When capRequestImages receives messages including tool-result images and their combined totals fit both request limits, then it returns the same array instance.

When imagesAsNotes receives a tool result with content "x" and a 640x480 PNG, then it returns that message with no images key and content equal to x
[image: image/png 640x480].

When estimateTokens receives a tool result with 400 characters of content and one image without dimensions, then it returns the estimate for the same result without the image plus IMAGE_TOKEN_ESTIMATE.

routing.reasoning: Crosses policy-sensitive tool execution and native session request seams, including error handling and audit timing; strict test isolation applies.

modifiedFiles.reason: the `runTool` entry for the tool runtime module is baselined at 24; if moving the outcome assembly into a helper lowers its score, the entry is lowered to the new score (an improved function keeps no slack), and no other entry changes.

userStories.title: Persist tool-result images in transcript sidecars
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Preserve native tool-result images across transcript saves and loads using the existing content-addressed sidecar.

**Motivation** — The image-attachments work (#2758, #2759) lets the user attach images to a user message; nothing lets the agent read one itself.

**Approach** — `splitTranscriptImages` and `rehydrateTranscriptImages` (`native/session/transcript-images.ts`) visit `tool-result` messages as well as `user` messages: a tool result's images are published to the same `<file>.images/` sidecar by content hash and stored as refs, the document is written with `schemaVersion: 2`, and loading rehydrates them inline. A document whose only images are on tool results is still split. A tool-result image whose sidecar file is missing is dropped on load and the same numbered line user messages get, `[image missing #<n>]`, is appended to that tool result's content, numbered by the existing `notedSlots` / `slotOf` logic; the tool-result stored arm goes through the same rehydrate loop as the user arm. `rehydrateTranscriptImages` scores exactly 20 (the strict limit) and has no baseline entry, so the per-message hydrate body (building `images`, the `notedSlots` / `slotOf` marker) moves into a helper scoring 20 or less, leaving `rehydrateTranscriptImages` no higher than today; no baseline entry is created for `transcript-images.ts`. A document with no images on any message is written unchanged, as today. Reuse `transcriptImagesPath` and the existing safe read/publish functions; the store must still publish JSON only after sidecar success. Extend `test/unit/native/session/transcript-images-write.test.ts` and `transcript-images-read.test.ts` including a store round trip.

**Scope** — In: the private stored representation and the native transcript store's existing save/load path for tool results. Out: native execution, image caps and compaction (US-002), file detection (US-004), provider mapping (US-001). Reading a transcript that has tool-result images with a build older than this feature: such a build passes the stored tool-result image refs through without `data`; the schema version stays 2. Showing tool-result images in the chat TUI transcript is out of scope.

**Interface**
```typescript
// StoredMessage tool-result arm
images?: readonly StoredImage[]
function splitTranscriptImages(path: string, doc: TranscriptDoc): Promise<unknown>
function rehydrateTranscriptImages(path: string, value: object): Promise<TranscriptDoc>
```
acceptanceCriteria: When splitTranscriptImages(path, doc) receives a document whose only image is a PNG on a tool-result, then it publishes the image under transcriptImagesPath(path) and returns a schemaVersion: 2 stored document with one image ref and no data on that tool result's stored image.
When rehydrateTranscriptImages(path, stored) loads that stored document, then the tool-result images equal the original [PNG A], including data.
When the same PNG bytes occur on a user message and a tool-result message, then splitTranscriptImages writes the image to the sidecar once.
When rehydrateTranscriptImages loads a document whose tool-result image file was deleted, then that tool result has no images key and its content ends with the line [image missing #1].
When splitTranscriptImages receives a document where no message carries images, then it returns the document unchanged, without adding schemaVersion: 2.
When a transcript whose tool result carries a PNG is saved and loaded through the transcript store, then the loaded tool-result message has the same images.

routing.reasoning: Extends an established persistence pattern while touching session storage and its filesystem trust boundary.

suggestedCriteria: When a tool result already has a trailing [image missing #1] marker and its first remaining sidecar image is missing on a later load, then the newly appended marker is [image missing #2].

userStories.title: Return image files from Read and clarify Bash wake behavior
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Have native Read emit supported image attachments and have the background-enabled Bash description tell the agent that task completion wakes it.

**Motivation** — The Bash tool already says `a notice arrives when the command ends`, but not that the notice wakes the agent, so it waited by hand.

**Approach** —

- New `packages/nax-agent/src/session/image-sniff.ts` holds `sniffImage`, `SniffedImage` and `ImageFormat` exactly as `packages/nax/src/chat/images/image-sniff.ts` defines them today (moved, not rewritten), exported from the `@nathapp/nax-agent` root beside the `image-input` constants.
- `Read` checks the file's leading bytes before its text path. When they match an image signature it returns an image result instead of text; any other file is read exactly as today. The decision is by bytes, never by file name. `readPrefix` decodes UTF-8 and cannot carry image bytes, so `packages/nax-agent/src/internal/bounded-io.ts` gains `readBytesPrefix(path, maxBytes): Promise<{ bytes: Uint8Array; size: number }>`: the same non-blocking open and regular-file check as `readPrefix` (a FIFO or a directory fails with `READ_NOT_REGULAR_FILE` as today), at most `maxBytes` bytes read, and `size` taken from the open handle's `stat`. The module's header comment, which says both helpers return up to `maxBytes + 1` bytes, is updated to describe `readBytesPrefix`, which returns at most `maxBytes`. The image branch lives in a new `packages/nax-agent/src/tools/read-image.ts` as `readImageResult(target, input, hasOffset, hasLimit): Promise<ToolResult | undefined>`, which never throws: a header or file read error (including `READ_NOT_REGULAR_FILE`) is returned as an `isError` result carrying the error's message. `readTool.run` scores 19 against the strict cognitive-complexity limit of 20, so its single call (`const image = await readImageResult(...); if (image !== undefined) return image;`) sits outside its `try`, after the credential refusal and after `parseRange` (an unsupported range alias such as `start_line` is still rejected first, image or not), and before the text branches; `readImageResult` itself stays at or under 20. Procedure: read a header of `IMAGE_HEADER_BYTES` (65,536) with `readBytesPrefix` and run `sniffImage` on it; no match means the text path. On a match, refuse when `size` is over 3,932,160; otherwise read the whole file (`readBytesPrefix(path, size)`) and run `sniffImage` on all of it for the dimensions. The image branch does not apply `ctx.maxFileBytes` (2,000,000 by default) or `readCeiling`; the image limit replaces them. Dimensions are kept only when both width and height are positive integers. An image result:
  - content `[image: <mimeType> <w>x<h>, <n> bytes]`, where `<n>` is the length of the whole-file read (the bytes that are base64-encoded), (`[image: <mimeType>, <n> bytes]` when the header gives no size, or a width or height that is not a positive integer, in which case the image entry has no `width` or `height`), `images: [{ mimeType, data: <base64 of the whole file>, width?, height?, source: <the path as given> }]`, not an error;
  - a file larger than `(MAX_IMAGE_BASE64_CHARS / 4) * 3` bytes (3,932,160) is an error with content `image too large to view: <n> bytes (limit 3932160)` and no images;
  - `offset` or `limit` on an image is an error with content `offset/limit apply to text files; "<path>" is an <mimeType> image`.
  - The credential read refusal still runs first, unchanged.
- `Read`'s description gains the sentence `PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP files are returned as images.`, inserted immediately before its closing `Output is capped at ...` sentence, so it still starts with `Read a UTF-8 text file from the repository.` and still ends with `Output is capped at 1000 lines or 40000 bytes.`
- `withBackgroundSentence` (`tools/bash-background.ts`) appends `Set "runInBackground": true to return at once with a task id; when the command ends, a notice wakes you with its result, so there is no need to wait or poll.` in place of today's sentence.

Move the sniffer test cases into `test/unit/session/image-sniff.test.ts`, without deleting the old nax files in this story. Add `test/unit/tools/read-image.test.ts` and update the pinned sentence constant in `test/unit/tools/bash-background.test.ts`, leaving those assertions otherwise unchanged. Regenerate `packages/nax-agent/api/nax-agent.api.txt` with `bun run api:update` from the agent package: only `ImageFormat`, `SniffedImage` and `sniffImage` are newly named on `.`.

**Scope** — In: named sniffer exports and API snapshot, bounded image reading on the policy-resolved target, Bash tool description, and corresponding tests in nax-agent. Out: the nax import switch and old copy's removal (US-008), transport/capping (US-001 and US-002), sidecars (US-003), and chat wake policy (US-005). ACP sessions are unchanged. Images from tools other than `Read` (Bash output, MCP tool results, embedder tools): only `Read` produces tool-result images. Showing tool-result images in the chat TUI transcript: the Read card shows the result's text line only. Resizing or re-encoding an image that is over the size limit: it is refused with an error, not shrunk. PDF, SVG, BMP, TIFF and HEIC files: only PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP are images to `Read`; other files take the text path as today. The Linux srt placeholder files (`.zshrc`, `.profile`, ...): tracked as #2986. The `nax-finish` skill's wording about background commands: changed in the nax-toolkit-skills repo, not in this feature.

**Interface**
```typescript
export type ImageFormat = "png" | "jpeg" | "gif" | "webp";
export interface SniffedImage {
  readonly format: ImageFormat;
  readonly mimeType: string; // "image/png" | "image/jpeg" | "image/gif" | "image/webp"
  readonly width?: number;
  readonly height?: number;
}
export function sniffImage(bytes: Uint8Array): SniffedImage | undefined
readBytesPrefix(path, maxBytes): Promise<{ bytes: Uint8Array; size: number }>
readImageResult(target, input, hasOffset, hasLimit): Promise<ToolResult | undefined>
function withBackgroundSentence(description: string, port?: BackgroundCommandPort): string
```
acceptanceCriteria: When sniffImage imported from @nathapp/nax-agent receives the bytes of a 100x50 PNG, then it returns { format: "png", mimeType: "image/png", width: 100, height: 50 }.
When sniffImage receives a GIF89a header carrying dimensions, then it returns format "gif" with the header's width and height.
When sniffImage receives a JPEG whose first frame marker is SOF0, then it returns format "jpeg" with the frame's width and height.
When sniffImage receives a VP8X WebP header, then it returns format "webp" with the header's width and height.
When sniffImage receives the bytes of the text hello, then it returns undefined.

When readTool.run reads a 100x50 PNG at shot.png without offset or limit, then it returns a result with no isError, content [image: image/png 100x50, <file size> bytes], and one image whose mimeType is image/png, width is 100, height is 50, source is shot.png, and data is the base64 of the file's bytes.
When readTool.run reads a JPEG, then the image entry's mimeType is image/jpeg.
When readTool.run reads a PNG stored as data.bin, then it returns an image result.

When readTool.run reads notes.png containing exactly the UTF-8 text `hello` without offset or limit, then it returns the unchanged text result `{ content: "[1 lines]\nhello", truncated: false }` with no images key.
When readTool.run reads a GIF whose header is too short to hold its size, then it returns content [image: image/gif, <file size> bytes] and an image entry with no width or height.
When readTool.run reads a 3,932,161-byte file starting with the PNG signature, then it returns { isError: true, content: "image too large to view: 3932161 bytes (limit 3932160)" } with no images key.
When readTool.run reads a file of exactly 3,932,160 bytes starting with the PNG signature, then it returns an image result.
When readTool.run reads the PNG shot.png with offset: 1, then it returns isError: true with content exactly `offset/limit apply to text files; "shot.png" is an image/png image`.
When readTool.run reads the PNG shot.png with limit: 10, then it returns isError: true with content exactly `offset/limit apply to text files; "shot.png" is an image/png image`.
When readTool.run reads a PNG with start_line: 1, then it returns the existing unsupported-argument error naming start_line, not the image error.

When readTool.run receives a directory, then the header read yields `{ isError: true, content: '"<resolved path>" is not a regular file' }`, preserving the existing READ_NOT_REGULAR_FILE message rather than exposing the exception.

When readTool.run receives a FIFO, then the non-blocking header read yields `{ isError: true, content: '"<resolved path>" is not a regular file' }`, preserving the existing READ_NOT_REGULAR_FILE message.

When readTool.description is read, then it contains `PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP files are returned as images.` immediately before the closing `Output is capped at 1000 lines or 40000 bytes.` sentence, preserving that ending and the opening `Read a UTF-8 text file from the repository.`.
When readTool.run reads a PNG whose header declares width 0, then it returns content [image: image/png, <file size> bytes] and an image entry with no width or height.
When readTool.run reads a 2,500,000-byte PNG with ctx.maxFileBytes set to 2,000,000, then it returns an image result.

When readBytesPrefix(path, 10) reads a 100-byte file, then it resolves to `{ bytes: <the first 10 raw bytes>, size: 100 }`, and when it receives a directory path it rejects with an exception whose code is `READ_NOT_REGULAR_FILE`.
When runtime.callTool("Read", { path: "shot.png" }) reads a PNG in the policy root, then it resolves to a kind: "ok" outcome with one image whose mimeType is image/png.

When withBackgroundSentence("Run a command.", port) is called with a background port, then it returns exactly: Run a command. Set "runInBackground": true to return at once with a task id; when the command ends, a notice wakes you with its result, so there is no need to wait or poll.
When withBackgroundSentence("Run a command.", undefined) is called, then it returns Run a command.

routing.reasoning: Adds bounded binary filesystem I/O behind a credential-sensitive Read path, a public export, and runtime integration; strict test isolation is required.

suggestedCriteria: When Read is asked for an image at a protected credential path, then it returns the existing credential refusal with no images key.
When Read receives a WebP or GIF file with valid magic bytes and positive integer dimensions, then the image it returns has the corresponding MIME type and dimensions.

modifiedFiles.reason: the names-only public snapshot of the `.` entry gains `ImageFormat`, `SniffedImage` and `sniffImage`; regenerated with `bun run api:update` from the nax-agent package directory. `ToolResult`, `CodingToolOutcome` and `AdapterInteractionResponse` appear by name only, so their new fields change nothing else.

the expected sentence constant at line 66 pins `a notice arrives when the command ends.`; it becomes `Set "runInBackground": true to return at once with a task id; when the command ends, a notice wakes you with its result, so there is no need to wait or poll.`, and the assertions that use it are otherwise unchanged.

userStories.title: Default chat task auto-wake to unlimited
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Deliver ended background-task notices without a consecutive-turn cap by default while retaining explicit positive caps.

**Motivation** — An agent working through a chain of background tasks the user approved stops at the fourth.

**Approach** — `chatTaskNoticeTurns` keeps its schema range (integer 0–100) and changes its default from 3 to 0 in `InteractionConfigSchema` (`config/schemas-infra.ts`) and in the `interaction` default object (`config/schemas.ts`). `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_TASK_NOTICE_TURNS` becomes 0. In `useJobs`, a limit of 0 never holds a task notice; a positive limit holds as today. This bypasses only the consecutive task-turn cap: a pending steer still owns its notice, and ordinary idle, in-flight, and notice-priority rules still apply. `taskNoticeHeldLine(limit)` keeps only its `auto-wake paused after <limit> task turns in a row` form; the `auto-wake is off` form is removed, because no setting turns auto-wake off any more. The field description becomes `Ended background-task notices that may wake the chat agent in a row before the user sends a message (0 = no limit)`. Update the comment in `config/runtime-types.ts` to `(default: 0 = no limit)` and update the default assertion in `test/unit/chat/chat-host.test.ts` and both defaults in `test/unit/config/schemas-infra.test.ts`, keeping range assertions unchanged. In `test/ui/chat/task-notices.test.tsx`, mount the three tests around lines 139–184 that rely on 3 with `taskNoticeTurns` 3 explicitly. Repurpose the old zero-as-off and marked-output-read hold tests to mount with a limit of 1 after one task-woken turn and use `taskNoticeHeldLine(1)`. Keep 0 in the AC-23/24 and AC-14 steer cases; check `taskNoticeHeldLine(1)` instead of the vacuous `taskNoticeHeldLine(0)` in the pending-steer case. Cover explicit and omitted unlimited limits, positive holds and resume/reset.

**Scope** — In: chat task-notice schema and host defaults, CLI field description, idle guard and held wording, and their config and TUI regression tests; keep the busy steer and explicit positive-cap paths. Out: changing the Bash tool description (US-004) or changing footer rendering (US-006). A setting that turns chat auto-wake off entirely: `0` now means no limit, and no value means never.

**Interface**
```typescript
// Resolved interaction field
chatTaskNoticeTurns?: number
export const MAX_CONSECUTIVE_TASK_NOTICE_TURNS = 0;
function taskNoticeHeldLine(limit: number): string
```
acceptanceCriteria: When NaxConfigSchema.parse({}) returns config, then interaction.defaults.chatTaskNoticeTurns equals 0.
When InteractionConfigSchema.parse({ defaults: {} }) returns config, then defaults.chatTaskNoticeTurns equals 0.

When FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS["interaction.defaults.chatTaskNoticeTurns"] is read, then its exact value is `Ended background-task notices that may wake the chat agent in a row before the user sends a message (0 = no limit)`.
When MAX_CONSECUTIVE_TASK_NOTICE_TURNS is imported from @/tui/chat/use-jobs, then it equals 0.

Given a chat mounted with taskNoticeTurns: 0, when a user sends one message and six background tasks end in sequence, each after the previous notice turn finishes, then send is called seven times and no transcript row contains auto-wake paused.

Given a chat whose host omits taskNoticeTurns, when a user sends one message and six background tasks end in sequence, each after the previous notice turn finishes, then all six notices are delivered the same way: send is called seven times with no auto-wake paused row.

Given a chat mounted with taskNoticeTurns: 3, when four background tasks end in a chain without an intervening user turn, then three notices are delivered, the fourth is held, and background task ended · auto-wake paused after 3 task turns in a row · send a message to continue is drawn exactly once.
Given a held notice with taskNoticeTurns: 3, when the user types a message and its turn ends, then the held notice is sent.
When taskNoticeHeldLine(2) is called, then it returns background task ended · auto-wake paused after 2 task turns in a row · send a message to continue.
Given taskNoticeTurns: 0, when a task ends while a turn is running, then the notice is steered into that turn and its steered row is drawn, as with a positive limit.

routing.reasoning: Changes defaults and one existing guard without adding a queue or changing the asynchronous delivery and steer mechanisms.

Also: the two tests that mount with `taskNoticeTurns` 0 to mean "hold every notice" ("a taskNoticeTurns of 0 never wakes the agent but still announces the held notice" at lines 194-199, and "a marked output read retires a held notice" at about line 580) now get no limit; each mounts with `taskNoticeTurns` 1 after one task-woken turn so the guard holds, and references to taskNoticeHeldLine(0) in them become taskNoticeHeldLine(1). The steer tests "AC-23/24" and "AC-14" keep `taskNoticeTurns` 0 and still pass; the vacuous taskNoticeHeldLine(0) check in "AC-14" (about line 470) becomes taskNoticeHeldLine(1).

the default assertions at lines 148-149 expect `chatTaskNoticeTurns` 3; they expect 0. The range assertions are unchanged.

userStories.title: Underline and accent the clickable footer strip
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make the jobs and tasks strip look clickable without changing its text, width or click target.

**Motivation** — A left click on the strip already opens the lone shell's output or the jobs picker (#2952, `footerStripHit` in `tui/chat/use-jobs-opener.ts`), but the strip is drawn as plain text, the same as the model name beside it.

**Approach** — `Span` (`tui/chat/styled-line.tsx`) gains `readonly underline?: boolean`, and `spanProps` passes it to Ink's `Text` `underline` prop. The strip's span is drawn `{ text, color: "accent", underline: true }` in every place it is built: `rightSegments` (`tui/chat/footer-segments.ts`), the summarised replacement in `summarised` (`tui/chat/status-layout.ts`, text `<n> active (ctrl+g)`) and `footerModel` (`tui/chat/chat-status.ts`). The separator after the strip and every other footer span keep their style. The strip's text and width do not change, so `stripWidth` and the click hit-test are unaffected. `sameStyle` and `styleOf` in `tui/chat/wrap.ts` enumerate the style keys; both gain `underline`, so a span that is wrapped, cut or merged keeps it. Extend the existing StyledLineView render test and footer-segments, status-layout and chat-status-tasks suites.

**Scope** — In: span styling, style retention and every form of the strip. Out: changing notice behavior (US-005) or rendering Read images in the TUI transcript. Live views of a running shell, a background shell or a subagent run (a shell details panel, a full subagent chat view): separate work. Existing click geometry and opener behavior stay unchanged.

**Interface**
```typescript
// Span
readonly underline?: boolean
// Strip span
{ text, color: "accent", underline: true }
```
acceptanceCriteria: When StyledLineView renders [{ text: "1 shell", underline: true }] and the same line without underline, then it writes the first line with terminal underline style and the second without it.
When fittedFooterModel receives one running shell task on a wide row, then its right-line span with text 1 shell has color "accent" and underline true.
When fittedFooterModel receives one running agent task, then its 1 agent span has color "accent" and underline true.

When fittedFooterModel fits a wide row with `jobs: [{ kind: "run", target: "demo" }]` and one shell task, then the `run demo · 1 shell` strip span (unchanged text for a run without progress or cost) has color "accent" and underline true.

When fittedFooterModel fits a wide footer with a `run demo · 1 shell` strip followed by model and cost, then the separator immediately after the strip retains color "muted" and has no underline, and neither the model nor the cost span has underline.

When fittedFooterModel fits the existing `TWO_JOBS_AND_A_TASK` fixture at 60 columns from `footer-fit-pipeline.test.ts`, a row narrow enough to summarize the strip, then its `3 active (ctrl+g)` span has color "accent" and underline true.
When fittedFooterModel receives no jobs and no tasks, then it returns no span with underline true.
When fittedFooterModel shows the strip for one running shell, then stripWidth equals the display width of 1 shell, unchanged from today.
When footerModel from @/tui/chat/chat-status receives one running shell, then its right-line 1 shell span has color "accent" and underline true.

routing.reasoning: One optional style propagated through five existing rendering and style helpers, without layout or input changes.

suggestedCriteria: When adjoining spans differ only by underline, then wrapping or cutting the line preserves the underline boundary instead of merging it into plain text.

userStories.title: Forward native tool-result images in run and hop sessions
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Carry the native coding tool's image list through the interaction handler shared by `nax run` stories and hop sessions.

**Motivation** — The image-attachments work (#2758, #2759) lets the user attach images to a user message; nothing lets the agent read one itself.

**Approach** — `buildRunInteractionHandler` (`packages/nax/src/agents/run-interaction-handler.ts`) maps a `CodingToolOutcome` to `{ answer: outcome.content, finalizeAudit? }`; it also copies a non-empty `outcome.images` onto the response through a helper `imagesField(outcome)` in the same file (`{ images }` when non-empty, `{}` otherwise; scoring 20 or less), so the call site gains only `...imagesField(outcome)`. `onInteraction` is baselined at 52 in `packages/nax/scripts/baselines/complexity-baseline.json`, and the helper keeps it from growing, so a `Read` of an image in a `nax run` story or a hop session reaches the model the same way it does in chat. Add the cases to `packages/nax/test/unit/agents/run-interaction-handler.test.ts`; retain existing audit, error, denied, and non-coding-tool behavior. Make `imagesField` directly importable by its unit test from this module, not from a package barrel. The call site is after the denied-outcome return, and actual error outcomes from the runtime have no images.

**Scope** — In: the non-empty image projection in the run/hop coding-tool response, the same-file helper, and handler regression tests. Out: the chat interaction handler and cap/compaction seams (US-002), producing images in Read (US-004), transcript sidecars (US-003), and vision negotiation (US-001). ACP stays unchanged, and context tools do not gain images.

**Interface**
```typescript
function buildRunInteractionHandler(options: RunInteractionOptions): InteractionHandler
// AdapterInteractionResponse addition supplied by US-002
images?: readonly ImageAttachment[]
```
`imagesField(outcome)` returns `{ images }` when non-empty and `{}` otherwise.
acceptanceCriteria: When the handler from buildRunInteractionHandler receives a coding-tool request whose runtime outcome is { kind: "ok", content: "x", images: [PNG A] }, then it answers { answer: "x", images: [PNG A] }.
When that handler receives a coding-tool request whose runtime outcome is { kind: "ok", content: "x" }, then its answer has no images key.
When imagesField receives { kind: "ok", content: "x", images: [] }, then it returns {}.

When the handler from buildRunInteractionHandler receives a coding-tool request whose runtime outcome is { kind: "error", content: "ENOENT" }, then it answers { answer: "ENOENT" }, preserving the existing error-text response without an images or denial marker.

routing.reasoning: A small additive mapping in one source file, with strict isolation because it touches the run/hop session interaction seam.

userStories.title: Use one shared image sniffer in nax
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Switch nax's attachment path to the agent's shared sniffer while keeping the `@/chat` API stable.

**Motivation** — The image-attachments work (#2758, #2759) lets the user attach images to a user message; nothing lets the agent read one itself.

**Approach** — `packages/nax/src/chat/images/index.ts` re-exports `sniffImage`, `SniffedImage` and `ImageFormat` from `@nathapp/nax-agent`; `image-file.ts` imports `sniffImage` from `@nathapp/nax-agent`; `packages/nax/src/chat/images/image-sniff.ts` and its test file are deleted (the test cases moved to nax-agent in US-004). `@/chat`'s exports keep their names, so `use-image-attach.ts` and `mention-expand.ts` are unchanged. Import the `SniffedImage` type from the same package as the function. Deletion-only apart from the two import lines; verified by `bun run typecheck` in `packages/nax`. The two specified PNG cases and the non-image refusal guard describe existing behavior. Use the `@/chat` attachment suite for regression verification; `imageFromBytes` takes `(bytes, source)` and returns `{ image }` or `{ refusal }`.

**Scope** — In: nax import/re-export redirection, removal of the obsolete local implementation and direct-import test, and verification of the existing `@/chat` attachment behavior. Out: changing sniffing or creating its agent export/tests (US-004), changing attachment validation or callers, and changing any model, session or persistence behavior (US-001–US-003 and US-007).

**Interface**
```typescript
export { type ImageFormat, type SniffedImage, sniffImage } from "@nathapp/nax-agent";
function sniffImage(bytes: Uint8Array): SniffedImage | undefined
```
acceptanceCriteria: When sniffImage imported from @/chat receives the bytes of a 100x50 PNG, then it returns { format: "png", mimeType: "image/png", width: 100, height: 50 }, preserving the existing export behavior.

When imageFromBytes imported from @/chat receives the bytes of a 100x50 PNG and source "clipboard", then it returns the success arm `{ image: ... }` whose image has mimeType image/png, width 100 and height 50, preserving the existing attachment behavior.

When imageFromBytes imported from @/chat receives the UTF-8 bytes of `hello` and source "clipboard", then it returns `{ refusal: "not a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image" }`, preserving the existing non-image refusal.

routing.reasoning: A small multi-file dependency cleanup crossing the public package boundary, with no algorithm or user-visible behavior change.
routing.noTestJustification: This is a structural relocation: the exact sniffer and its direct tests move to nax-agent in US-004, and this story changes only imports/re-exports and removes the duplicate files. The existing @/chat regression assertions and package typecheck verify the migration without new runtime behavior.

modifiedFiles.reason: deleted: it imports the nax copy of the sniffer, which this story deletes, and its cases now live in the nax-agent sniffer test that US-004 creates.

analysis:
This is an enhancement to the existing TypeScript/Bun workspace, not a new architecture. Preserve the dependency direction nax-ai → nax-agent → nax, Node-compatible source in nax-ai and nax-agent, and no changes to nax-agent-acp. The graph MCP was unavailable, so repository findings were confirmed with targeted text search and direct reads. Sequence: US-001 defines the wire contract for US-002; US-003, US-004 and US-007 then build on US-002; US-008 follows US-004. US-005 and US-006 are independent. Done means a native Read of a supported image flows through chat, run and hop, is bounded and persisted, and reaches a vision model or yields an explanatory note on a text-only model. The bundle also changes the task-wake default, Bash guidance, and the visual affordance of the footer without changing click behavior.

US-001 — Wire: packages/nax-ai/src/protocols/types.ts:123 already defines shared ImageAttachment and :150 is the text-only tool-result arm. packages/nax-ai/src/protocols/pi-client.ts:143 maps conversation messages, :197 recovers a tool name from an earlier assistant call and rejects orphan results, and :223 exposes toPiContext. Keep the lookup, timestamp and isError behavior; only change tool-result content projection. User images are currently ordered before text and omit empty text; do not reuse that ordering for tool results. pi-ai is pinned to 1.5.0 at packages/nax-ai/package.json:38; the spec relies on its existing provider routing for tool-result image blocks, not a new provider integration. Capability belongs at the current-model boundary so replay after switching models can degrade without changing history. Strip local image metadata at that boundary. The supplied isError-plus-image mapping criterion tests an independently supplied protocol message; it does not authorize an errored native tool to emit images. Extend the Vitest user-image fixture at packages/nax-ai/test/protocols/pi-client-images.test.ts:7 and preserve tool naming/error regressions at packages/nax-ai/test/protocols/pi-client.test.ts:106. These fixtures prove message mapping, not live provider behavior.

US-002 — Native transport: packages/nax-agent/src/tools/registry.ts:21 defines ToolResult; packages/nax-agent/src/tools/runtime.ts:64 and :439 define the outcome and assemble it after policy execution. The immediate path records audit before returning, while deferred truncation returns an audit callback; preserve both, along with sandbox metadata, policy access checks, error handling and cancellation. The file is 599 lines and runTool's current baseline is 24 (packages/nax-agent/scripts/baselines/complexity-baseline.json:15); reuse the existing extraction module (packages/nax-agent/src/tools/runtime-calltool.ts:1), which deliberately imports runtime types only, and lower the runTool baseline to its new score if it drops. Use the existing type re-export in packages/nax-agent/src/cost/standard-types.ts:9 outside native code. The production chat backend constructs the session interaction handler at packages/nax-agent/src/session/native-backend.ts:160, whose answerFor maps denials, throws for errors and currently projects only successful text and sandbox metadata (packages/nax-agent/src/session/session-interaction.ts:301). Add images at that seam and in packages/nax-agent/src/session/interaction-handler.ts:35. The embedder path in session-interaction.ts:199 remains textual. packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/turn-tool-batch.ts:274 shapes text and finalizes audit before calling the shared builder in packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/tool-result.ts:26; its catch path at :307 must remain image-free. The plugin whitelist in packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/loop-events/registry.ts:68 stays unchanged: images travel beside the patch, not in it. The turn event uses only the text preview (packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/turn-event-emitter.ts:140); no card/event image payload is needed. packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/turn-loop-round-trip.ts:310 consumes the batch; packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/turn-complete-step.ts:168 already caps the wire copy, and packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/turn-compaction-step.ts:123 already hands note-only input to the summarizer. Extend the user-only branches at packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/image-context.ts:5 and :20 and the native transcript arm/estimate in packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/compaction.ts:24 and :57. Use one newest-first budget for both roles (20 images and 20,971,520 base64 characters, packages/nax-agent/src/session/image-input.ts:8), keeping original order for survivors and original array identity when nothing is dropped. Avoid mutating history, leaking base64 into text, or treating image char counts as text tokens; use the existing dimension-based estimate and 1,600 fallback. Existing runtime, turn-tool-batch, image-context and image-compaction suites cover the seams. Use the real handler/runtime composition in packages/nax-agent/test/unit/native/session-adapter-abort-reasons.test.ts:184 as the template for the new two-round-trip integration fixture.

US-003 — Persistence: packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/transcript-images.ts:32 models only user sidecar refs; :104 preflights MIME types and then publishes images before JSON, and :224 hydrates only user messages. Reuse existing content-addressed publishing and hydration, not a second store or schema. The actual directory is <file>.images/ with .json replaced, as implemented by transcriptImagesPath at :40. Preserve atomic publication, MIME/ref validation and path/symlink/regular-file safeguards at :53, :132 and :158. Share hydration and missing-slot bookkeeping (notedSlots and slotOf at :193 and :209) so repeated save/load after loss keeps original numbering. The existing store calls hydrate at packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/transcript-store.ts:67 and split at :73, so no caller rewrite is needed; extend the transcript-images-write/read suites, including the real store seam (write suite :166). Existing imageless and user-image documents need no migration; only saves with images use schema 2 and no new version is introduced. Downgrade to a build that cannot hydrate tool-result refs is unsupported. Keep current safety regression tests and complexity limits.

US-004 — Read and Bash: packages/nax-agent/src/tools/read.ts:75 defines the tool text, :99 resolves the policy-provided target, :105 checks credentials before input range parsing (:112), and :116 begins the existing text path. Keep that order; do not open a protected path just to sniff it. packages/nax-agent/src/internal/bounded-io.ts:24 opens non-blocking, checks the opened handle, and uses one overshoot byte for text; the binary reader has a hard cap without the overshoot. The extra header probe also touches non-images, so retain text behavior, normal error messages, and bounded allocation even if the file changes between reads. Report actual bytes encoded, not the first stat size. The existing sniffer at packages/nax/src/chat/images/image-sniff.ts:1 and :85 recognizes by magic bytes and does not decode pixels; copy unchanged into nax-agent in this story, then remove the old copy in US-008 so each package remains buildable between stories. Raw image cap is 3,932,160 derived from MAX_IMAGE_BASE64_CHARS (packages/nax-agent/src/session/image-input.ts:7); it replaces the text read ceiling only for images, not the permission decision. Keep the existing text tests in read-cap.test.ts, the non-regular-file regression in packages/nax-agent/test/unit/tools/buffering-ceilings.test.ts:103 and credential regressions in packages/nax-agent/test/unit/tools/credential-read-deny.test.ts:79. Regenerate the names-only root API after adding the named exports beside image-input at packages/nax-agent/src/index.ts:416. Bash composes its description via withBackgroundSentence at packages/nax-agent/src/tools/bash.ts:400 and packages/nax-agent/src/tools/bash-background.ts:172; change only the sentence for port-enabled backgrounding and the expectation in bash-background.test.ts.

US-005 — Configuration and behavior: packages/nax/src/config/schemas-infra.ts:117 and packages/nax/src/config/schemas.ts:318 both default to 3; packages/nax/src/chat/chat-host.ts:155 forwards the resolved value. Update both defaults, the fallback at packages/nax/src/tui/chat/use-jobs.ts:16, descriptions at packages/nax/src/cli/config-descriptions.ts:285 and the runtime-types comment at :244. The idle effect in use-jobs.ts:201 prioritizes run asks then jobs then task notices, counts only delivered task turns, and noteUserTurn at :275 resets the counter; the busy steer path is separate. Preserve those rules, queue/dequeue and held-line deduplication. Omitted or explicit 0 becomes unlimited; there is no off-mode migration. Users wanting the previous default cap can set 3 explicitly, and existing positive values remain unchanged. Retarget tests that implicitly used 3, convert old 0-as-off cases to a positive cap after a prior wake, and exercise default/explicit unlimited chains, user reset and busy steering in packages/nax/test/ui/chat/task-notices.test.tsx:139, :194, :369 and :463. Align the schemas-infra and chat-host default tests.

US-006 — Rendering: packages/nax/src/tui/chat/styled-line.tsx:17 defines the span and :71 translates its style tokens into Ink props. packages/nax/src/tui/chat/wrap.ts:66 and :102 compare and preserve style, including across grapheme fragments. The strip has three constructors: packages/nax/src/tui/chat/footer-segments.ts:73 for wide fitted footers, packages/nax/src/tui/chat/status-layout.ts:50 for the narrow replacement, and packages/nax/src/tui/chat/chat-status.ts:292 for the legacy model. Do not style the separator or other spans. status-layout.ts:63 computes text display width for the hit target; packages/nax/src/tui/chat/use-jobs-opener.ts:41 and :102 use the same geometry. Existing status-layout, footer-segments, chat-status-tasks, wrap and use-jobs-opener tests cover layout and click semantics. packages/nax/test/ui/chat/styled-line.test.tsx:24 provides an Ink render fixture; assert underline under a terminal style configuration that actually emits it. No layout, persisted setting, theme token or mouse migration.

US-007 — Run/hop: packages/nax/src/agents/run-interaction-handler.ts:60 and :84 implement the alternative native interaction handler used by packages/nax/src/runtime/session-run-hop.ts:162 and packages/nax/src/operations/build-hop-callback-hop.ts:330. Copy the non-empty image list alongside answer and audit callback, retaining denial, error text, cancellation and context-tool behavior. Keep the branch condition in imagesField so onInteraction stays within its current baseline of 52 (packages/nax/scripts/baselines/complexity-baseline.json:21). Extend packages/nax/test/unit/agents/run-interaction-handler.test.ts:23; the two existing consumers need no wiring changes.

US-008 — Migration to one sniffer: packages/nax/src/chat/images/index.ts:10 and packages/nax/src/chat/images/image-file.ts:2 currently import/re-export the local copy; the public barrel at packages/nax/src/chat/index.ts:99 already exposes the names. packages/nax/src/tui/chat/use-image-attach.ts:32 and packages/nax/src/chat/mentions/mention-expand.ts:13 consume those exports and need no rewiring. Keep the attachment flow's independent size and pixel-edge checks in image-file.ts:36 and move only the sniffer implementation/tests. The import in packages/nax/test/unit/chat/images/image-file.test.ts:3 is already through @/chat and is the regression home for both behavior checks. Delete the nax-local source and direct-import test only after US-004 adds the root export and moves its cases. Verify the migration with the package typecheck as an implementation check, not a behavioral criterion. No version bump, external dependency change, transcript conversion, or consumer import migration is needed.
outOfScope: ACP sessions (Claude Code, Codex, opencode through nax): they read images with their own tools; nothing in `packages/nax-agent-acp` changes.
Images from tools other than `Read` (Bash output, MCP tool results, embedder tools): only `Read` produces tool-result images.
Resizing or re-encoding an image that is over the size limit: it is refused with an error, not shrunk.
PDF, SVG, BMP, TIFF and HEIC files: only PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP are images to `Read`; other files take the text path as today.
Showing tool-result images in the chat TUI transcript: the Read card shows the result's text line only.
A setting that turns chat auto-wake off entirely: `0` now means no limit, and no value means never.
Live views of a running shell, a background shell or a subagent run (a shell details panel, a full subagent chat view): separate work.
The Linux srt placeholder files (`.zshrc`, `.profile`, ...): tracked as #2986.
Reading a transcript that has tool-result images with a build older than this feature: such a build passes the stored tool-result image refs through without `data`; the schema version stays 2.
The `nax-finish` skill's wording about background commands: changed in the nax-toolkit-skills repo, not in this feature.
